# Base58

Base58 in the Bitcoin alphabet, which leaves out look-alike characters.

<h2 id="base58-encoded-max-length"><code>Base58EncodedMaxLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Base58EncodedMaxLength(length: uint) -> uint
```

The most characters the Base58 form of `length` bytes can occupy.
Each byte needs at most log 256 / log 58, about 1.366, digits, so this is a bound rather than the exact length,
which depends on the value. A destination of this length is always enough. Cannot fail for any length a slice
in memory can have; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Base58.rux#L51)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type   | Description                   |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `length` | `uint` | the number of bytes to encode |

**Returns**: an upper bound on the number of characters [`Base58Encode`](/docs/api/encoding/base58#base58-encode) writes

<h2 id="base58-encode"><code>Base58Encode</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Base58Encode(
    bytes: byte[..],
    into: var char8[..]
) -> uint ! FormatError

pub func Base58Encode(
    text: char8[..],
    into: var char8[..]
) -> uint ! FormatError
```

Writes `bytes` as Base58 into the front of `into`.
Runs in time quadratic in the length of `bytes`, and not in constant time. Reports `InsufficientCapacity` when
the encoded form does not fit `into`; `Base58EncodedMaxLength(bytes.length)` characters always fit. A refusal
leaves `into` filled with zero bytes, because the conversion used it as scratch space. Room past the encoded form
is not touched on success.

| Overload                                                                            | Summary                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Base58Encode(bytes: byte[..], into: var char8[..]) -> uint ! FormatError` | Writes `bytes` as Base58 into the front of `into`.             |
| `pub func Base58Encode(text: char8[..], into: var char8[..]) -> uint ! FormatError` | Writes the bytes of `text` as Base58 into the front of `into`. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Base58.rux#L64)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type            | Description                    |
| ------- | --------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `bytes` | `byte[..]`      | the bytes to encode            |
| `into`  | `var char8[..]` | the destination                |
| `text`  | `char8[..]`     | the text whose bytes to encode |

**Returns**: the number of characters written

<h2 id="base58-decode"><code>Base58Decode</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Base58Decode(
    text: char8[..],
    into: var byte[..]
) -> uint ! DecodeError
```

Reads Base58 text in the Bitcoin alphabet into the front of `into`.
Each leading `1` becomes a zero byte. Runs in time quadratic in the length of `text`, and not in constant time.
Reports `InvalidCharacter` at the first character outside the alphabet, leaving `into` untouched, and
`InsufficientCapacity` when the decoded value does not fit `into`, leaving it filled with zero bytes because the
conversion used it as scratch space. The count carried by that refusal is a lower bound on the length needed,
not the exact length; `text.length` bytes are always enough.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Encoding/Src/Base58.rux#L141)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type           | Description               |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]`    | the Base58 text to decode |
| `into` | `var byte[..]` | the destination           |

**Returns**: the number of bytes written
